sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text: Avana has demonstrated real relay/panel production growth, with a space-led factory expansion rather than a speculative new product story. BQS 5.50 and Growth Quality GQS 6.55 reflect credible scaling but only moderate cash and capital quality. At the dated ₹162 quote, a funded central case earns about 2.17% annually versus a 15% analyst hurdle, giving IAS 3.225. The business can improve while the share disappoints. This is conditional research, not a buy or sell instruction.

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: As of 20 October 2026, NSE SME AVANA was listed on January 20, 2026. October 19 is the latest completed quote session because October 20 is a holiday. Official close ₹162 and 22,645,408 shares imply ₹366.8556 crore equity value; a 2,000-share lot costs ₹324,000 before charges. Standalone FY2026 annual accounts and the January 14 prospectus supply the baseline. All four gates are assessed below: integrity and accounting pass with specific caveats, funding passes conditionally, and investability is conditional on lot/ASM constraints. An unmodified audit is not blanket assurance. [S1, S2, M1]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Canonical factors are GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 5, BAL 7, EXEC 6 and EARN 6. BQS uses the prescribed weights and totals 5.50; GQS totals 6.55 without a cash/capital cap. IAS uses Q 5.50, R 1, D 4, P 3 and L 4, totaling 3.225. Central IRR 2.17% minus the 15% hurdle is −12.83 percentage points. All factors are Medium confidence, with explicit history ceilings; no probabilities are invented and no score is withheld merely because future forecasts are uncertain.

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text: Avana designs and manufactures control/relay panels, protection relays, substation automation and SCADA, with testing and commissioning support. FY2026 domestic product revenue ₹83.1592 crore, exports ₹0.4628 crore and services ₹0.2368 crore demonstrate predominantly Indian equipment economics, not recurring software revenue. Purchased components and engineering/assembly make space and execution important; the prospectus says existing machinery will move to the new site without major machinery additions. Two rented facilities are to consolidate on KIADB lease land. [S1, S2]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Product approvals, engineering integration and field reliability can support repeat business, but no verified pricing-power or retention series establishes a durable moat. FY2025 top-five/top-ten customer shares were 22.42%/31.50%; the September 2025 half-year rises to 38.79%/52%, showing order lumps. Danish Power and Aartech are useful operating references, not identical businesses. Danish FY2026 consolidated sales ₹521.45 crore and CFO ₹42.50 crore come with ₹74.15 crore capex; Aartech’s dated FY2025 operating EBITDA was negative despite positive PAT. These contrasts argue against valuing all electrical companies with the same P/E. [S2, P1]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Revenue in FY2023–26 was ₹28.4065/52.9877/61.4858/83.8588 crore: three-year CAGR about 43.4%, with FY2024–26 about 25.8%. Four annual observations are not a five-year/full-cycle record, so Medium-confidence REV is capped at 8 rather than 9–10. FY2023–25 relay production rose from 27,942 to 58,501 to 65,840; panels from 478 to 502 to 523, corroborating real volume. Six months to September 2025 produced 33,650 relays and 313 panels; these are half-year quantities, not annual capacity utilization. FY2026 PAT ₹11.7228 crore rose 38.4%, but restatement, warranty and diluted-share effects limit extrapolation. [S1, S2]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The proposed factory raises annual relay capacity from 70,000 to 175,000 and panel capacity from 600 to 1,500. FY2025 utilization was about 94.06% and 87.17%, giving a practical reason for expansion. August 19 says the new unit was nearing completion and production was expected by end October, not already commissioned. FY2026 capex ₹7.5023 crore and CWIP ₹4.6679 crore are actual; remaining commitment ₹10.9499 crore is funded explicitly in the model. Incremental NOPAT/deployed-capital proxy is about 20.5%, falling to 8.8% when all current cash is retained as committed; warranty normalization lowers them to about 13.8%/5.9%. This range supports moderate CAP, not a proven project return. [S1, S2, S6]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: FY2026 four-director pay ₹2.8948 crore plus relatives’ consulting ₹0.78 crore totals ₹3.6748 crore, 31.3% of PAT. However, total director pay fell from FY2025 ₹3.404 crore including ₹1.55 crore incentives, so salary-only growth would mislead. September 28 approved annualized FY2027 director pay ₹3.4164 crore; promoter votes were counted and approval is not independent minority endorsement. The annual report allocates company IPO expenses ₹4.9809 crore and discloses promoter OFS recoveries. The utilization certificate’s ₹5.5101 crore is not fully reconciled merely by that allocation; the valuation reserves the difference. Bank-reported receivables exceeded books by 2.15–7.77% in FY2026 quarters, labeled not material by management; request reconciliation rather than infer wrongdoing. [S1, S3, U1] The April 8 declaration, filed June 9, records 16,675,408 promoter/group shares, about 73.64% at March 31. Its exception for previously disclosed encumbrances is not a blanket zero-pledge certificate. [S7]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text: Annual FY2025/26 CFO ₹5.7322/7.9544 crore gives two-year CFO/PAT 0.678; FY2026 cash after capex is only ₹0.4521 crore. Inventory rose ₹7.723 crore, receivables ₹1.022 crore and payables financed ₹4.0166 crore. The restated FY2025 CFO difference ₹1.0344 crore is offset by short-advance investing reclassification; margin-deposit cash-pool changes explain the remaining cash difference. Cash/bank ₹27.8278 crore includes ₹7.1917 crore restricted margins and ₹2 crore other deposits. Receivables over six months ₹3.0713 crore include ₹0.311 crore over three years, all considered good. Warranty opening ₹4.3199 crore plus ₹0.4181 crore additions less ₹1.5165 crore utilization equals ₹3.2215 crore; this is not evidence of an improper release. Expense/material overlap remains a normalization uncertainty, tested explicitly. [S1, S2, U1]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At ₹162, reported full-share EPS about ₹5.18 implies 31.3 times FY2026 earnings. The central case uses 15% sales growth, 16% normalized economic EBIT margin and 12 times terminal EV/EBIT; it pays the factory commitment, taxes, issue reserve, debt principal and interest, and funds working capital from the first month. It yields about 2.17% annual equity return, versus bear −17.99% and bull 18.08%. The new model does not multiply NOPAT by an equity P/E: terminal EV is bridged through debt, legacy claims, excess cash and diluted shares. April–October is estimated from March actuals, not an assertion of current cash. Scenario detail, reverse expectations and 27 sensitivities are retained below. [S1, S2, S6, M1] Under central economics, a 15% hurdle corresponds to a conditional entry price around ₹89.67; at ₹162 it instead requires about 31.1% annual sales growth with the same normalized margin and terminal multiple. This is a model sensitivity, not a price target.

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Permanent loss can arise from a missed factory ramp, slower collections, warranty costs and valuation compression even without insolvency. The bear case remains funded but loses about 62.9% of entry value over five years. A zero-growth, 8% margin, 6 times EV/EBIT stress with 30% project overrun, all old receivables lost, extra warranty cost and no new credit requires about ₹2.06 crore rescue equity and loses about 85.2%. Bank guarantees ₹4.8142 crore and LCs ₹1.9616 crore are exposures, not automatically funded debt; crystallization needs separate analysis. Restricted margins are not freely distributed. ASM and large lots may frustrate an exit precisely during stress. [S1, M_ASM]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Five-year 5 times and 10 times per-share outcomes require 37.97% and 58.49% annual returns. The central case produces only about 1.11 times and the bull about 2.30 times; neither supports a five-year multibagger claim. Planned physical capacity is 2.5 times old capacity, not a guarantee of proportional revenue or owner value, and growth beyond the capacity-linked envelope requires additional capex. No unsupported probability is assigned.

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Monitor actual commercial production against the end-October expectation, relay/panel quantities and capacity utilization, sales margin after full director pay and warranty costs, inventory and ageing collections, IPO object utilization and the issue-expense bridge, restricted deposit release terms, and bank-versus-book receivable reconciliations. Escalate if commissioning slips without explanation, CFO/PAT stays below 0.6, old receivables grow faster than sales, or new funding is needed while cash is described as surplus. Refresh spread, depth, ASM and PAN breadth before any implementation. October 19 REG1 alerts apply to October 21, not retroactively. [S1, S6, M_REG1]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Completed conditional review: credible growth and expansion capacity, moderate governance/cash quality, and demanding price-implied expectations. BQS/GQS rankings are supported at Medium confidence; IAS is also scored conditionally rather than automatically withheld for forecast uncertainty. The price does not meet the central 15% hurdle. Actual commissioning, cleaner cash conversion and a less demanding valuation would change the assessment; none is assumed to have occurred.

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary sources include the annual audited accounts and notes, prospectus, signed exchange clarification/utilization certificate, AGM voting, board factory update and official market records. Units in lakh are divided by 100. Restated and annual scopes remain labeled; October operating balances are not observed. Open questions are exact commissioning, updated orders and product volumes, issue-cost reconciliation, warranty expense/material allocation, margin-deposit release and executable market depth. These are bounded through the funded scenarios where possible, not disguised as completed facts. October 16 price-query response is an issuer statement that no other unpublished information existed, not independent proof that the price move was fundamental. [S5]

All old receivables over six months lost

Issue cost reconciliation resolved without reserve

valuation.method: Monthly April 2026 opening through October 2031. Five-year investor horizon begins November 2026; first seven months are estimated. No dividends. EV/EBIT less actual and modeled debt and legacy claims plus excess cash. DTA and interest receivable excluded; no IPO proceeds credited again. Project commitment includes remaining IPO project allocation, not additive. Long warranty included in operating WC exactly once. All scenarios conditional, not forecasts of executable trades.

assumption_rationale.growth: 15% central growth is below FY24–26 25.8% and FY23–26 43.4%. It relies on the planned 2.5 times relay/panel capacity and existing volume/customer evidence, not an unverified order book. FY25 sales divided by 90% blended utilization times 2.5 gives about ₹170.79 crore capacity-linked sales; 3% annual mix/price growth is an explicit assumption. Any revenue beyond this envelope requires additional productive capex at 5 times incremental sales/capital. Physical product mix and productivity mean this is not a promised revenue ceiling.
assumption_rationale.margin: Central 16% economic EBIT margin is below FY26 18.48% excluding other income and retaining bank charges as operating expense. A prior warranty/sales normalization costs ₹1.2591 crore and approved director-pay increase costs ₹0.5216 crore, together implying about 16.35%; 16% allows a small additional execution buffer without claiming those adjustments are certain. No deposit interest or speculative rent saving capitalized.
assumption_rationale.multiple: Central 12 times EV/EBIT, bear 8 and bull 16 are analyst sensitivities, roughly 16.4/11.0/21.9 times unlevered after-tax operating earnings at 27% tax. They are not copied from stale peer P/Es. The current reported P/E is 31.3 times.
assumption_rationale.funding: ₹20.6361 crore opening cash includes ₹18.6361 crore cash equivalents and ₹2 crore non-margin deposits; the ₹7.1917 crore restricted margin pool is excluded. Unused IPO ₹21.0398 crore overlaps these balances and is never added again. Full remaining factory commitment ₹10.9499 crore is paid over the seven-month bridge, not added to the ₹8.7955 crore IPO project remainder. Current tax ₹2.1604 crore paid over 12 months. New credit limit 10% of revenue is an uncommitted assumption; no-new-credit sensitivity provided. Rescue equity at half the dated quote if needed.
assumption_rationale.timing: Actual opening March 31, 2026; April–October is an explicitly estimated bridge, not observed October balances. Five-year investor horizon November 2026–October 2031. Factory production expected end October per August 19 filing; no commissioning announcement found by cutoff. Bear adds a 12-month growth delay. No dividend was declared for FY26, and no forecast dividend assumed.
assumption_rationale.claims: Current statutory, employee, expense and customer liabilities and non-tax short provisions are included in opening and closing operating WC. Long warranty ₹2.5772 crore is operating WC too; sustainable warranty margin/provision assumption, not free surplus. Long employee ₹0.3669 crore reserved at terminal, with early-payment case. DTA ₹0.2527 crore and interest receivable ₹0.2495 crore receive no cash credit. Security deposits remain operating assets. No double deduction of these assets from actual cash.

valuation.issue_expense_caveat: Annual company issue cost ₹4.9809 crore versus utilization certificate ₹5.5101 crore leaves ₹0.5292 crore not fully reconciled; promoter OFS allocations alone do not prove the difference. A further ₹0.3045 crore certificate remainder produces a deliberately conservative ₹0.8337 crore reserve paid in the opening bridge. Release sensitivity bounds valuation effect. Not an allegation of misappropriation.

GOV.reason: Promoter remuneration and relatives fees substantial; shareholder approval counted promoter votes. Counterevidence: actual total director pay fell, OFS costs apportioned and disclosures detailed.

MOAT.reason: Engineering/approvals and actual capacity utilization support capability; customer/order lumps and competitive peers limit pricing-power proof.

REV.reason: FY23–26 three-year sales CAGR about 43.4% maps above 8 before the Medium-confidence history ceiling. Only four actual annual observations and no pre-pandemic full cycle; 9–10 not supported. FY24–26 25.8% and actual production corroborate persistence without cherry-picking the shorter window.

DUR.reason: Domestic grid demand and funded factory provide runway; near-full historical capacity necessitates execution, customer orders not permanent annuity.

CAP.reason: Economic incremental returns about 20.5% deployed versus 8.8% retaining committed IPO cash; warranty sensitivity 13.8%/5.9%. CAP 5 reflects capital still being deployed, not a mature return already achieved.

CASH.reason: Same-scope annual two-year CFO/PAT is 0.678, with positive but small FY2026 cash after capex. No financing is included in CFO; deposits reconcile, but inventory and receivable absorption remains material.

BAL.reason: Debt of ₹0.7614 crore against large cash provides a buffer, but restricted deposits, unused IPO commitments and guarantees prevent treating all cash as surplus.

EXEC.reason: Production and revenue expanded with debt reduction. The factory was nearing completion, not confirmed operational; commissioning and warranty performance need monitoring.

EARN.reason: Positive PAT growth and operating scale are supported, but warranty expense normalization, prior-period gratuity/leave and IPO dilution reduce extrapolation confidence.

R.reason: Central monthly equity IRR 2.17% minus 15% hurdle = −12.83 percentage points, R 1. No probabilities or assumed rerating are required.

D.reason: Bear terminal loss 62.9%; severe 85.2% with ₹2.06 crore rescue equity under no credit. Ordinary bear is cash funded, but shareholder-value loss is material.

P.reason: Current quote needs about 31.1% annual sales growth at central margin/multiple to earn 15%; central is 15%. Stronger growth and valuation persistence must coincide.

L.reason: 60-session conditional median ₹22.6075 lakh gives 4.42 days at 5%; 20-session fully observed median ₹25.107 lakh gives 3.98 days. Starting 7 reduced to 4 for ₹3.24 lakh lot, ASM, fewer than 100 PANs and unverified spread/depth. One absent August 25 record is not asserted as a proven zero-trade session.

gates.reason: No reviewed primary evidence establishes severe integrity failure. Related remuneration and repeated bank-versus-book receivable differences demand scrutiny; promoter-voted approval is not independent endorsement. No allegation inferred.

Annual cash identity and restated cash-pool/reclassification bridge reconcile. Warranty expense/material treatment, issue-cost difference and bank return mismatches are bounded and explicitly sensitized; they do not currently make the full annual baseline unusable.

Central and bear fund the project and legacy claims without new equity. Severe zero-growth/8% margin/overrun/receivable and warranty loss with no credit needs about ₹2.06 crore rescue; this is an identified stress vulnerability, not evidence of current default or a demonstrated ordinary-case unfinanceable shortfall.
₹324,000 lot, named short-term ASM and limited PAN breadth; observed turnover does not establish order-book exit. ₹500,000 reference cannot be implemented exactly: one lot ₹324,000, two ₹648,000.
